timestamp_derivation: After the navigation change, the settings relocation and the full UI suite passed; before the author timestamp of the commit that introduces this receipt. Per T0091, in the order T0108 requires.

change.navigation: PMS Reconciliation and Roster Reconciliation are no longer primary navigation items. Both remain routable and are reached from PMS connection under Advanced diagnostics.
change.attention: PMS connection now states whether reconciliation needs investigating, with a direct link when it does and an explicit nothing-to-do statement when it does not. This was the only thing an operator previously had to open a diagnostic page to learn.
change.settings_moved: The five connection-recovery bounds moved from Roster reconciliation to PMS connection -> Advanced configuration. They are configuration for the link, not diagnosis of it. The diagnostic page points at their new home.
change.docs: The operations manual and the standing-exception record now give the new location.

explicitly_unchanged: Reconciliation functionality, history, audit evidence, safeguards and backend behaviour; PMS semantics; the automatic reconciliation rules; guest and stay state handling; routing; security boundaries; permissions; and the distinction between operational outstanding work and historical or diagnostic records. Neither reconciliation process became a manual task.
deployment: NONE. No appliance deployment was authorised and none was performed. No PMS configuration or runtime change was made.
tests: 288 UI tests pass, including new assertions that both routes still exist while absent from primary navigation, and that the diagnostic page now carries no control.
